bug_semantics: MultipartFile.move(location, options) treats the attacker-controlled multipart filename as the destination basename. When options.name is omitted, the method defaults to this.clientName (the Content-Disposition filename) and builds the path with path.join(location, name) with no sanitization, prefix check, or basename() confinement. A crafted filename containing ../ (or an absolute path, which path.join can treat as the new root) writes the uploaded body outside the intended directory. After 900627c1500bb38155ee3f9620a89ed7609b996e the overwrite default is true, so an existing target is replaced. Reachable whenever an app calls move() without an explicit sanitized name.
flaw_origin: The current TypeScript sink was first written in 81eacb00a7cbad6d6a3eb964ea79e3e71b3ae394 (feat: add move method to the file instance). That commit added File.move() with options = Object.assign({ name: this.clientName, overwrite: false }, options) then this.filePath = join(location, options!.name!). The 2019 rewrite had deleted the prior JS File.move; the parent tree's src/Multipart/File.ts has no move method. Later commits only refactored the same default (overwrite flipped to true in 900627c; path rename; merge restore) until the 2026 patches stopped using clientName as the default name.
